problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{7x-1}{3{x}^{2}-2}.$

feedback.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{4}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{4},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{3{x}^{3}-{x}^{5}}{2{x}^{4}+{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3{x}^{3}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{x}-x)}{(2+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{3}{x}$ and $\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{3}{x}-x)}{(2+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ≈\frac{0-x}{2+0} \\  & =-\frac{x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This is not a constant, which means that $y=f(x)$ does not have a horizontal asymptote.
